newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel says banks approve safety moves.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel says banks approve safety moves.

text.p: Lending banks to Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc have been advised of the company's package of safety measures unveiled on Thursday and approve them, British co-chairman Robert Malpas said.
Malpas told Reuters on the margins of a news conference at the Calais terminal of the tunnel, "the banks' response is approval. They think we are on the right lines."

He said Eurotunnel is in constant touch with the steering group representing its 225-strong loan syndicate and had given details of the new procedures and measures, which involve spending around an extra 20 million pounds ($32.8 million) on new equipment.
On top of the capital expenditure, mostly to set up six fire-fighting stations inside the tunnel, extra staffing and training would involve between one and 1.5 million pounds a year.

Eurotunnel was confident the safety authorities would approve the restart of the Shuttle freight service in the "next several weeks" and allow a full commercial service by June, Malpas said. "We are not studying contingency plans", he said when asked of the possibility of a delay in approval.
"Yes, it is critical for us to restart this service as soon as we possibly can," he said.

Eurotunnel is due to hold an annual general shareholders meeting by the first week of July, he said. It hopes to get approval by a two-thirds majority of shareholders for a restructuring of some 70 billion francs of junior-ranked bank debt. The deal involves a swap of eight billion francs of debt for equity.
"By the annual general meeting, we expect all of this to be behind us," he said.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 0.609 British Pounds)
